\section[cancelar]{cancelar — to cancel, to call off}

\label{lesson:PT-C372-cancelar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the unexpected problem, then the Portuguese for the alternative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cancelar}
\textbf{cancelar} — \textquotedblleft{}to cancel, to call off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cancelaram o concerto por causa da chuva.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They cancelled the concert because of the rain.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Cancelar uma reserva} — to cancel a booking.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cancelar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cancellāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make like a lattice\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{cancellī} \textquotedblleft{}a lattice, bars\textquotedblright{}: a cancelled text was crossed out with lines.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cancelar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cancelar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{cancelar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the unexpected problem, then the Portuguese for the alternative, then say \emph{cancelar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does cancelar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cancel, to call off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[adiar]{adiar — to postpone, to put off}

\label{lesson:PT-C372-adiar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the alternative, then the Portuguese for to cancel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: adiar}
\textbf{adiar} — \textquotedblleft{}to postpone, to put off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Adiámos a viagem para setembro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We put the trip off until September.}
\end{quote}

European \emph{adiámos} (past) beside \emph{adiamos} (present). \emph{Adiar para} — to put off until.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{adiar} is built on \emph{dia} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{diēs} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the prefix \emph{a-}: to put to another day.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adiar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adiar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{adiar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the alternative, then the Portuguese for to cancel, then say \emph{adiar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does adiar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To postpone, to put off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[provisório]{provisório — provisional, temporary}

\label{lesson:PT-C372-provisorio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to cancel, then the Portuguese for to postpone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: provisório}
\textbf{provisório} — \textquotedblleft{}provisional, temporary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Este horário é provisório.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{This timetable is provisional.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A título provisório} — provisionally.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{provisório} is built on \emph{provisão} \textquotedblleft{}provision\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{prōvīsiō} \textquotedblleft{}a foreseeing\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{prōvidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to foresee\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[definitivo]{definitivo — final, definitive}

\label{lesson:PT-C372-definitivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to postpone, then the Portuguese for provisional.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: definitivo}
\textbf{definitivo} — \textquotedblleft{}final, definitive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A data do casamento ainda não é definitiva.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The wedding date is not final yet.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Em definitivo} — for good.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{definitivo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēfīnītīvus} \textquotedblleft{}definitive, explanatory\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{dēfīnīre} \textquotedblleft{}to set bounds\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{fīnis} \textquotedblleft{}boundary, end\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[flexível]{flexível — flexible}

\label{lesson:PT-C372-flexivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for provisional, then the Portuguese for final.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: flexível}
\textbf{flexível} — \textquotedblleft{}flexible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu horário é flexível: posso entrar às dez.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My hours are flexible: I can start at ten.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Horário flexível} — flexible working hours.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{flexível} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{flexibilis} \textquotedblleft{}that may be bent, pliant\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{flectere} \textquotedblleft{}to bend\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
